text.p: Following are reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Reform Party denies rumours its ministers intend to resign from the government on Friday. Party secretary Heiki Kranich said they would decide if they will stay in the coalition at an assembly on November 1.

- Estonian and Latvian presidents signed a declaration on bilateral cooperation for gaining security, growth of stability and prosperity, and admittance to European and Trans-Atlantic political, economic and security structures.
- Estonia and Russia were considering new proposals for formulating the Tartu Peace Treaty in the bilateral border agreement, Estonian Ambassador to Russia Mart helme said.
- Central election commission has rejected two protests over slight violations at the recent local council elections.
- First Estonian court case over kidnapping began on Wednesday in Tartu. The defendant Margus Sippol pleaded guilty and expressed regret at kidnapping a four-year-old boy.
- Political will was needed for forming a Baltic customs union, Latvian Economy Minister Guntars Krasts said in Tallin.
- Privatisation Agency Council has decided to sell 29.3 percent of shares of gas company Eesti Gaas for privatisation vouchers by a public auction.
- Centre Party leader Edgar Savisaar is negotiating with various political parties on a coalition for Tallinn City government.
- New Estonian cultural award, the URSA MAJOR, was established Wednesday with first prizes to be announced December 28.
- Hansa Bank intends to sell its 32 percent of the Savings Bank shares. Swedish Sparbanken is one of the potential buyers.
